reviews.text: 最近新出的骰子类游戏是真的多，加上前段时间类宝可梦游戏大火，骰子+宝可梦这俩也能缝到一起我是没想到的。 玩法上招募3个宝宝组队冒险，搞装备给他们上强化，通过骰子发动攻击或者换位防御，通一把1小时熟练后一把应该40分钟左右，右上角有动画加速打到一半才看到。 大体上游戏还是不错的，有一点不是很满意，新招募的宝宝会顶掉以前的宝宝，直接就给顶没了，为什么不搞个口袋把换下来的宝宝存起来需要的时候在换上场，在一个为什么不给宠物分个属性比如火系、水系、草系之类的，互相之间有克制，在给宠物上个羁绊哪些一同上场会触发羁绊效果给一些额外属性，不要多一点点就好，真的我觉得真的可以搞一搞。
神骰鬼脸 O(∩_∩)O~ 太好玩辣！

目前来说，游戏性还可以，前几局还算有趣，但瑕疵太多，目前不建议购买 很想退款但是不小心超过2小时了。 ----------------------------- 问题出在哪呢？ 这游戏有大量需要对局经验解锁的宝宝 但是初始可选宝宝只有十来个，并且有很多无用技能，再加上局外无成长，初始难度始终一致，全看三选一给什么宝宝，起手第一张图选不到实用的基本宣告结局 然后，一共三个宝宝位置，但每张图都只能三选一，就算加上卷轴，卷轴没得选，只有那一个，还是大概率给垃圾 ——最后就是玩的时候大部分战斗都是在用初始宝宝，第一第二次玩还好，后面就非常无趣。 相比之下，前几周出的那个元素骰子，虽然也是局外无成长+大量复杂的解锁道具，但在无解锁情况下可用牌数量非常之多，废牌数量也远小于实用牌，基础套路是非常容易成型的，比这个舒服很多 这游戏我和朋友同一时间玩的，选出来的阵容基本一致 第一把运气好通关了，第二把试了下风暴，起手给了三坨屎直接放弃思考了 ———— 局内成长性也很差，大部分buff都是“仅回合内有效”，单回合能做的操作又非常有限 boss机制反而是永久性的，就很奇怪 到最后三图自己全队20来血对面全是60血起步 自家攻击力基本个位数，装备配好的才能2位数 对面怪要机制有机制要血量有血量 第三章，160血的boss，三只怪一个比一个逆天，冰冻我受伤翻倍，灼烧我受伤增加，专注他攻击翻倍，你搁这一刀修罗呢 妈的，三配合阵容每回合打5刀+11点回合结束回血，最后被打到差点寄了，靠20%概率连A三刀才勉强拿下 --------- 最后，我的修改建议是增加每张图的可招募次数（比如取消卷轴，将招募地点从3个降低为2个，但每次都有不同的3选1），增加地图大小或者增加到4-5个章节，并且替换的宝宝不消失，而是提供3个暂存位置，选择使用永久增加属性道具的时候可以选择后备宝宝。。
玩法好评，但宠物的设计太糟糕了 好用的宠物能打100分的话，那得有大量的宠物连及格分都达不到，弱到看见就想重开。 游戏里还有大量的鸡肋装备（比如必须被击杀后才能生效），制作组对于内容设计的问题真的不小。
画风不错，玩法有创意，但可惜作为一款肉鸽深度不够而且几乎没有局外成长不耐玩

It pains me but since Steam doesn't have an option for neutral review I guess I'd have to leave a negative one. The main reason for it being - game simply lacks depth and variety. Despite there being so many different chimeras, different factions with supposedly different playstyles your run would pretty much always look the same. You're always looting the whole map, you're always buying your two die In shops, you're pretty much doing the same stuff on the battlefield - attack and spin, well maybe sometimes more inclined to spinning over attacking and vice versa. Runs just don't feel different enough: - you don't get enough decisions; - chineras mostly split in two categories - bad and good ones, not really considering your build; - item pool is pretty small and I feel like every run I'd see more than 50% of the pool; - no rarity or tiers for items (like boss specific f.e.) makes very unexciting to get one too; Balancing the game with very little decision to make also makes your game really easy - you pretty much can't fail making a build and only can die to execution error. And sure there is trial mod (aka ascensions) which are byw done in a cool manner when enemies become stronger but you also get benefits. But by the time of this review I've beaten trial level 6 and haven't lost a single time (11 or 12 wins back to back). That being said I do want to highlight that on all the other fronts game is really nice - most charming artstyle, comfy music, lots of little animations for different debuffs, like sleeping states drawn for every chimera! Or every chimera making a unique sound taking damage. You can really see lots of loved poured into the project and I do appreciate it. But still it's a GAME. And most important thing in a game will always be gameplay. Which feels shallow and lacking - its like there is missing a system or two to seal the deal and make the game really great.

--2024.3.3-- 这是一个很棒的游戏，画风精美且机制新颖，但我不得不提出关于这个游戏中存在的一些严峻问题： 1. 不同奇美拉之间的效果差距太过明显，有的奇美拉很强，有的奇美拉则需要很严苛的配合才能产生效果，还有的奇美拉甚至毫无用处。 此处我需要着重提及苦痛护符，携带此护符所能吸引的奇美拉需要受到伤害或攻击盟友才能起效，问题是，对盟友的攻击代价过大，如果说一次标准行动所能产出的收益是100，那么一个好的奇美拉的效果能将这次的收益变成200（例如镰刀鼬和彩虹三头鸡），但是如果我花费一个行动攻击队友，就会产生-100的赤字，那么奇美拉产生的效果至少因该是300，而实际上现版本中经常连到达200都很难，例如豹蟒，它的效果是攻击队友后会攻击对方全体，他产生了的效果就只是300-100=200，并且在高难度下，击败boss不会回复血量，这令它的运用变得困难，豹蟒每上升1点力量，都意味着队友会受到更加恐怖的伤害，我在一局游戏中养出了一只50HP的爪鲸鱼，专门让它挨打，但效果很差。 重点来了，更令人惊讶的是，所有被攻击时产生的效果都能对队友发动，这意味着那些能让攻击自己的人产生DEBUFF的奇美拉效果和装备与“进攻队友的流派”之间完全不兼容，但这类效果的奇美拉和装备的数量却很大，荆棘会让队友承受巨大的伤害，棒球棍攻击队友会让队友产生流血，爪鲸鱼让豹蟒获得了专注，但豹蟒却不能再次攻击爪鲸鱼，否则爪鲸鱼便会承受双倍伤害，这些到底是什么鬼？我敢说你们根本没好好测试这个护符中奇美拉的兼容性。 2.刚才说到了荆棘，我确实通过荆棘通关过高难度，但它真的很难用，不管是荆棘、混乱还是流血，它都依赖于敌方的行动，但敌方的行动是不稳定的，我很难让敌方多次位移，也难以承受被多次攻击的代价，而流血更是在只剩一个敌人时毫无用处，这使得这些被动效果难以被主动运用，我认为在这款游戏中，即使是被动的效果也因该是能被主动运用的，它得足够有攻击性，而不是仅仅作为辅助，不然我为何不专注于力量与攻击呢？ 3.许多装备的效果简直是一团狗屎，抱歉。请问在高难度中，每个敌人在开局时都带有护卫的情况下，一件能让持有者开局攻击一次的道具有什么作用？在敌方骰子耗尽时能造成6点伤害的装备，面对几百血的敌人时有什么作用？还有每回合对自己造成1点伤害的道具，噢，我明白它有用，但就像我之前说的，我希望得到100，而这个道具给了我-50，也许这个道具配合一些奇美拉的效果能获得100，但也不过就是-50+100=50，为了这个效果我得让队伍的血量不断下降，你不觉得把这个道具的效果改成“受到1点伤害然后回复1点HP”会让它变得更加有效吗？ 4.我相信上述提到的很多问题你们也已经发现了，在优先修改那些问题之后，我希望还能有以下改进： -商店可以花费金钱刷新。 -不要再让灌木丛出现在通往神龛的路上。 -减少诅咒装备的数量，并加强其效果，易损坏装备也一样。 -增加回复生命的手段。 -彩虹奇美拉的效果很强大，我希望能减少自然产生的概率，同时增加一些能让玩家主动将普通奇美拉变为彩虹奇美拉的机会，例如在最终boss前，玩家可以选择一只奇美拉变为彩虹，哪怕只有一次机会。我相信让玩家能自己选择强化哪只奇美拉，会对游戏体验产生很大的帮助。 -还有很多问题...或许我之后会补充。 Translation software: --2024.3.3-- This is a great game with a beautiful art style and novel mechanics, but I have to raise some serious issues about this game: 1.The difference in effectiveness between different Chimeras is too obvious. Some Chimeras are very strong, some require strict coordination to produce results, and some Chimeras are even useless. I need to emphasize the Painful Talisman here. The Chimera that can be attracted by carrying this Talisman needs to take damage or attack allies in order to take effect. The problem is that the cost of attacking allies is too high. If a standard action can produce a profit of 100, then a good Chimera effect can turn this profit into 200 (such as the Sickle Weasel and the Rainbow Three headed Chicken). However, if I spend one action attacking teammates, it will generate a deficit of -100, so the Chimera effect should be at least 300. In reality, in current versions, it is often difficult to even reach 200, such as the Panther Python, which attacks the opponent's entire team after attacking a teammate, resulting in a deficit of -100. The effect of Leopard Python is only 300-100=200, and in high difficulty, defeating the boss will not restore health, making its use difficult. Every 1 point increase in strength of Leopard Python means that teammates will suffer even more terrifying damage. In one game, I raised a 50HP Claw Whale specifically to make it vulnerable, but the effect was very poor. The key point comes, and what's even more surprising is that all the effects generated when attacked can be unleashed on teammates, which means that the Chimera effects and equipment that can make attackers DEBUFF are completely incompatible with the "attacking teammate genre". However, the number of Chimera effects and equipment for such effects is large, thorns can cause huge damage to teammates, baseball bats can cause teammates to bleed, claw whales can focus leopard pythons, but leopard pythons cannot attack claw whales again, otherwise claw whales will suffer double damage. What the hell are these? I dare say you haven't tested the compatibility of Chimera in this talisman properly. 2. As I mentioned earlier, Thorn is indeed too difficult for me to pass through, but it is really difficult to use. Whether it is Thorn, Chaos, or Bleeding, it depends on the actions of the enemy. However, the actions of the enemy are unstable, and I find it difficult to make them move multiple times, nor can I bear the cost of being attacked multiple times. Bleeding is useless when there is only one enemy left, which makes it difficult to actively apply these passive effects. I believe that in this game, even passive effects should be able to be actively applied. They need to be aggressive enough, not just as auxiliary. Otherwise, why don't I focus on strength and attack? 3. The effect of many equipment is simply a pile of dog poop, sorry. What is the purpose of a prop that allows the holder to attack once at the beginning of a high difficulty game, where each enemy is accompanied by a guard at the beginning? What is the effect of equipment that can deal 6 damage when enemy dice are depleted when facing enemies with hundreds of health? There are also props that deal 1 point of damage to themselves per turn. Oh, I understand they are useful, but as I mentioned before, I hope to get 100, and this prop gave me -50. Perhaps this prop, combined with some Chimera effects, can get 100, but it's only -50+100=50. For this effect, I need to keep the team's health decreasing. Don't you think changing the effect of this prop to "take 1 point of damage and then restore 1 point of HP" will make it more effective? 4. I believe that you have also discovered many of the issues mentioned above. After prioritizing the modification of those issues, I hope to make the following improvements: -Stores can be refreshed with money. -Don't let the bushes appear on the way to the shrine again. -Reduce the number of cursed equipment and enhance its effectiveness, and the same applies to easily damaged equipment. -Increase the means to restore health. -The effect of Rainbow Chimera is very powerful, and I hope to reduce the probability of natural occurrence, while increasing some opportunities for players to actively turn ordinary Chimera into Rainbow Chimera. For example, before the final boss, players can choose a Chimera to turn into Rainbow, even if there is only one chance. I believe that allowing players to choose which Chimera to strengthen on their own would greatly benefit the gaming experience. -There are still many questions Perhaps I will add it later.

It gets very repetitive very fast. The fixed factions make the build archetypes per playthrough feel very static compared to other roguelikes that let you pick fully random teams. In 4 hours I beat the game with all of the main 4 factions and then secret 5th faction, but have no desire to do the "Trials" with the same fixed monster pool. I wouldn't say this game has high replayability once you've unlocked each faction's full roster unless you REALLY like the roster each faction is limited to.

10月更新评价，垃圾制作组请所有人别买这游戏。 2月发布的游戏，本来是个挺好的底子，但游戏内有一大堆问题（见下面我之前写的评测），结果制作组整整半年就发布了3个补丁修改了些不痛不痒的问题。游戏还是一个几乎是测试版的残废游戏，然后制作组一点内容修改和添加没有，在8月就出付费DLC了。 别买！！！！ ========================================================== 一个失败的rogue游戏，或多或少会有这三点特征：随机带来的负反馈太强、局外成长解锁的越多游戏体验越差、需要玩家反复刷开局。很不幸，这三个特征在这个游戏上集齐了。 虽然rogue游戏不免会有一些负反馈，但这游戏的负反馈也太强了。我辛辛苦苦爬到三层，把背包和果子都养给了一个宝宝，结果第三层开出来了一个一样的宝宝还是闪卡，这时候我换不换都会觉得血亏。再比如前两层都没成型，结果第三层给我开出了三个废物宝宝，不但没得换，已经很亏了，但看完这三个宝宝的窝，我又亏了两个废墟的收益，亏上加亏。类似于这种“屋漏偏逢连夜雨”的情况还有很多，就导致游戏经常是好不容易游戏进入到了后期，但是接踵而至的负反馈导致体验差的一比。 目前的整局游戏偏短，选择的容错率很低，但在这种情况下又塞入了大量需要“体系”去支撑的构筑，比如“活化”和“法术”，而这两种体系除非特别胡，否则基本比不过各种堆力量的平A流，直接导致了解锁的宝宝越多，没用的废物就越多，进一步降低体验。 以及我认为任何需要“刷开局”的肉鸽游戏做的都很差，但这个游戏经常要刷开局，比如灌木丛帐篷之类的格子踩上去了就必须马上获取，但有时候这些格子挡在去拿宝宝的路上，我又不能把这些收益放在注定要被替换掉的三个初始宝宝身上，只能重开。我不明白在目前选择本就少的可怜的情况下，这游戏为啥会有单行道走格子这种设计。 目前的体验来看，构筑也很难，职业几乎没啥用，整个队伍的构筑都是围绕着第一层能拿到的两个宝宝来进行的，而不是职业。 制作组得好好想想怎么才能减少一些负反馈，比如如果三个祭坛开出的都是废物没法拿的情况下，给与玩家一些正反馈的激励，比如直接升级一个宝宝变成闪卡。 DEMO玩了很久，很上头，游戏也能看出来是用了心的，但目前的游戏体验我只能给个差评。
差评来自蓝面猴蝠（盟友加力量时随机攻击）+剑鱼兽（盟友攻击时攻击）携带恶魔斧（攻击时提升力量）无法无限连。你要么设置道具的时候写清楚并机制上规避无限连的情况，要么就是我拿到了就给我爽完这一把，天胡爽玩是肉鸽的一环，不爽不要做肉鸽。

Dicefolk is a game that immediately attracted for its gameplay and cute artstyle when I play the demo. The fact that you also select what the enemies dices does and can try to mitigate damage and other negative effect that way is so clever. I was also always a fan of dice game and throwing dice so getting to personalise the dice face was also a joy. Unfortunately, as you can see with my playtime, I barely played 4 hours and I'm already getting bored. Simply put, there is not enough variety for a rogue like. Neither with enemies, your own chimera(the little pokemon-type creatures that fight for you), nor with objects. Then there the fact that many chimeras simply sucks. Not only because many of them are just straight up bad but others also only shine in a specific team composition. If you don't have the chimeras that synergize with them, many of them become useless, which dwindle an already limited pool of creatures. The second stage is especially difficult because it contain so many bad chimeras. I know luck play a role in all rogue-like, but never I restarted so many runs because of bad rolls on chimeras and object. The fact that apart from unlocking new things you don't really get to progress between the runs reinforce that feeling of luck dependence, since that normally how those games balance this aspect. Play the demo, see if you like the gameplay, and then decide if you can play this, and exactly this(with very few upgrades and evolution), for the next ten hours or so. Otherwise, I would suggest to play something else.

Really absorbing game with fresh new mechanics and game play. It stay interesting from beginning to end. Pretty unforgiving game play but not that hard if you take the time to plan your moves. Great for casual and hard-core gamer's. Worth the money? Yes, it is. One of your better indie titles and belongs in your library. Oh, and it works perfectly on the steam deck. Sorry, I can't think of any cons.

[h1]Simple Concept, Crazy Synergies, Brutal RNG[/h1] For me, this game has the same problems and fun factors as Wildfrost. [h1]Things I Like About Dicefolk:[/h1] [b]1. Simple and Fun Gameplay[/b] Gameplay of Dicefolk comprises two parts: rotation and dices. It is important to rotate your team to deal the maximum amount of damage and manage each chimera's health carefully. It is also important to do the same thing to your enemies, but in reverse! This is where Dicefolk gets interesting. Not only do you need to use your dices wisely, but you need to waste enemies' dices as well. You can only end the turn when you exhaust all enemies' dice, so carefully managing each dice is key to success. [b]2. Lots Of Crazy Synergies[/b] There's many [strike]pokemons[/strike] [strike]digimons[/strike] [strike]monsters[/strike] [strike]coromons[/strike] [strike]cassette beasts[/strike] chimeras in the game. Each of them has a unique trait which aims to synergize with others to create the ultimate team dynamic. Things like damaging enemies on rotation, auto-attacking when entering lead, or granting ally buff when attacked, the list goes on and on. Each chimera can equip up to five equipments, further making the synergies ridiculous. I still remember my cactus spider keeps tanking for the team while three ghost boi and a green onion with scarf keeps buffing and healing him. In the end, my boi gets like 120 Thorn buff(deal damage when hit) that anything touches him will immediately die. [b]3. Other Compliments[/b] →Love the art style. →The chimeras look so silly, I love them!! →Boss fights are fun to work around their gimmicks. [h1]Thing I Dislike About Dicefolk:[/h1] [b]Brutal RNG[/b] The same problem happened to Wildfrost happens in Dicefolk as well, at least for me. so much potential but just not quite there. for context ive finished the game and am climbing through the tiers of the trial difficulty. it really is a great game concept but as a someone whos looking for a roguelike experience this genuinely feels like an early access game when it comes to the roguelike elements and specifically around the lack of build defining choices. The core gameplay is great - lots of thought provoking decision making in the moment to moment combat. The art and music are captivating and really engaging. However I have had considerable issue with the lack of variety in this game. The classes have their own list of chimeras and each of them are clearly at different powerlevels. This issue is exacerbated with how you only have the option of having 3 of them within your party and only get to pick a single one from each area (there is one more way to pick but it's utterly random from the roster). This means that most of the time you will resort to a no brainer pick when presented with options (This includes equipment as you will likely see over 60% of the options in each run). This results in many runs effectively being the exact same thing - which to be honest isn't a bad thing but with the way the classes are structured - despite the massive roster of creatures - everything will feel samey because you will always pick the safe options when presented with so little choices. To the developers - you have built a fantastic foundation but please continue to work on the class system and overall roguelike decision making. I would personally suggest removing the class locked systems altogether to give players more variety and instead have classes based around starting game defining equipments or special dices specific for that class. Another option would be the idea of being able to collect more creatures but being able to swap them in and out or even being able to select your three creatures from the start to let players focus on equipment (can add rarities, an upgrade system etc). Lastly please consider add rerolls of some kind to shops - i've had many runs where I've been bricked trying to run a mana build without getting a single mana dice or mana items (This just makes certain archetypes unplayable) until the 2nd or 3rd area of the game. I would love to continue playing this game if these issues are addressed! This really hurts because to be honest - the game is so unique but I just can't recommend the game for players like me who are invested in this genre as the lack of variety utterly ruins the experience given the price point. In saying that - if you are looking for a casual roguelike game and this looks appealing to you please don't let this deter you!

I'm a bit pained to leave a negative review for this. It's cute, it's got creatures that you collect, it's very evocative for the first few hours, BUT it's missing the heart of what makes a good roguelike. The other negative reviews have been accurately pointing this out and the devs either won't or can't make the changes necessary to really shake the game up and make it into a much better game. Primarily, it still feels like it's in early access with major issues that remain unaddressed: * difficulty is too low and the final boss is laughable (the fight before him is almost always much harder) * there are no 'decisions' during the run - you see everything and get everything * creatures and items are in no way balanced with a few 'good' ones and a wide array of useless * the item pool is incredibly limited and not tiered (you'll see the same drops over and over) * run difficulty is determined by the RNG favoring you with 'good' or 'bad' creatures and stores * the different "creature family" talismen wind up feeling very similar * the spinning mechanic seems like it will be pivotal (ha) but you use it less and less once you get your team set up The core concept is good, but the execution is not. That said, the game is still enjoyable. It's got charm. It's got decent creature visual design. If you're not deep into roguelikes, you may even love the game. As such, I'm going to say: vets of roguelikes: 5/10, newbies or creature collector fans: 7-8/10.

半夜想评价一下这款游戏。 总体来说，对于宝可梦或者怪物对战的爱好者来说可以原价入，不然还是等打折吧。 本人还没买DLC，但是原游戏最高难度通关，目前正在打挑战，被气的过来写这个评论。 游戏的优点在于可玩性是足够的，奇美拉跟装备和骰子的配合很有趣，也有构筑深度。并且奇美拉的设计我很满意，虽然不是萌系画风但是设计感十足。 但缺点依然很明显：奇美拉的强度过于不平衡，导致很多看上去很酷炫的奇美拉沦为花瓶。而游戏的奇美拉选择也给的不多，如果要逛满三个神龛意味着舍弃金钱和回复奖励，还要清掉道中的杂怪。而在高难度的环境下，仅靠初始怪的强度而缺少回复，打完一层boss也只会复活回到1滴血，这样战损的积累是致命的。 就很容易陷入一种恶性循环：想要避免战损 → 需要赌到强力怪 → 开更多的神龛而舍弃金钱和回复奖励 → 没钱买好装备和骰子 → 战损扩大。 而奇美拉之间技能的差距几乎可以到完爆的程度：比如某个怪的技能是特定情况下攻击力翻倍，一回合一次。而另一个怪的技能是攻击时会攻击两次…… 当然官方为了平衡，很细心的设计了面板差异。 看起来解决了一些平衡问题，但也带来了新的问题：面板差强力技能的怪需要养成才能carry起来，不然后期拿到会因为面板太低而效果不好。 另一个问题是奇美拉之间的互动过少。有的玩家可能会反驳说：明明奇美拉的技能设计了不少联动啊！但问题在于奇美拉的强度差距过大，导致几个二三流的怪配合起来过关还磕磕绊绊，打个boss像要解道高数题。而强力的奇美拉就可以靠装备和骰子的配合几乎单刷boss，最多选点回复和辅助伤害的队友，但是配合感远远比不上技能联动的奇妙反应。 综上，高难过关很大程度上就是在赌一个强力奇美拉carry全场。好在游戏难度不高，非最高难度下队伍差一点也能过关。但还是有些攻击队友才能发动效果的奇美拉实在鸡肋……还得专门配自由攻击的骰子面，然后还需要急缺的回复，真是白瞎了那么好看的造型。 所以建议官方在新增武器和奇美拉的同时，把奇美拉的强度平衡一下。不用削强的，至少把弱的加强成能用。比方说某个被打才能加攻的鳄鱼我实在不知道怎么用，但你把他改成扣血加攻立马就能用了，虽然仍旧不是很强。

Man, this is a tough one. It is a good game, chimeras are well balanced, there are different strats and builds to mess around for a bit. Main mechanic of controlling both yours and your opponen's actions is clever. That said, the game has 2 big cons for me: 1) There just isn't enough variety for a game of a genre like this one. I gets repetitive pretty fast. No big decisions to be made, no events that shake things up a bit. Once you see all he faactions and enemies, runs get pretty similar from each other. 2) The game is very, very easy. If you are a rogue like vet like me, you will probably not lose a single game. I have played 12 and haven't lost yet. Ascensions give you boh a penalty and a benefit, so the game doesn't get much harder either. As a result, I'm in a place where the only purpose of playing is to unlock every chimera and item, while I keep climbing the ascensions in the hope that, at some point, the game actually gets a bit more challenging, having not much fun in the process. I do like that there are many things to unlock, but if the difficulty is a cakewalk it just feels like a chore to me. It would have been much better to have less things to unlock (meaning more in the base game) but with an earlier ramp up in the difficulty that made the game more fun and challenging. As it is, the game seems much more enjoyable for people that come for the creature collection aspect that for fans of roguelikes. It also seems more appropiate for players not familiar with this genre, given how easy it is. But for people that are searching for a replayable and challenging roguelike to put a lot of hours in, there might be better options around there.

Dicefolk is a mobile app that's been dumped on Steam as if it was a real PC game (it's not)... it's a cash grab from greedy mobile devs. This mobile app is <<<<<< ABOOOUUUUUUT >>>>>> This mobile app is at a core level, a very lazy ripoff of Slay the Spire with cartoony anime reject artwork, and a mechanic where the CCG aspect of the game (you know, the best part) is replaced with a crappy "action dice" mechanic... and weirdly, not quite understanding how dice games work, you have to roll the dice for the enemy, too. That's not fun, but this really feels like a half-baked "Let's make some money off the back of Slay The Spire's concept" cash grab more than anything serious for PC gamers... well, it is a mobile app first and foremost, and developers pushing mobile trash onto Steam for profit is not okay. But that's what's happened here. From a technical perspective, as a mobile app, this doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard. While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality. Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals. The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers, left handed gamers or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts. The game features no proper level design or game/story flow/plot, as they opted to try to use samey repetitive procgen algorithms as a substitute for adding such content to the game, to avoid doing the important job of level/map design. As a result, the game doesn't actually have any content worth mentioning, just endless, boring, repetitive, soulless algorithmically generated sameyness. Developers must learn that procedural generation is not an acceptable substitute for content. Because this is a mobile app, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies. Compromises were made to cater to the iPhones that the game was designed for. These are unfortunate handicaps and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was an afterthought for the iPhone developers who are to blame for this. The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for mobile phones forces upon a game. Once more, mobile devs have made gaming worse for everyone. I didn't spend thousands on building a gaming rig just so I could pretend it's an iPhone. These technical shortcomings push this mobile app below minimum standards for any competently developed modern PC game. Let's talk about price and the value this represents for us gamers. Should you buy this mobile app? Is it among the best the Steam catalogue has to offer? This happens far more often than it should. Greedy mobile devs are attempting to scam PC gamers. On Steam this costs $15 USD, yet on the app stores it's only $5 USD. That is THREE TIMES THE PRICE you can buy it for on the app stores. Mobile devs must learn PC gamers are not here to be gouged, and can't be expected to pay a premium for a mobile app just because it's been lazily dumped on Steam at an inflated price. This is unacceptable disrespect for PC gamers. This mobile app is being sold at a deliberately inflated price to try to scam PC gamers into paying more money than mobile gamers do for the exact same iPhone game. [i]They want you to pay $15 USD on Steam for a $5 USD mobile app!!![/i] Just who do they think we are?

Quite a fun game with incredible production values and glaring balance issues. By that I mean once you progress far enough into the challenges and difficulty, you'll frequently be faced with unwinnable scenarios based purely on how unlucky you were in the random application of the modifiers. An example would be getting stuck on a boss that requires you to kill its two mobs in order for it to take any damage at all, but both mobs getting hit with a status that makes them untargetable until the targetable enemy is destroyed (in this case, the boss, randomly selected, which cannot be directly damaged). It absolutely still gets a recommend from me. There's a very good amount of fun to be had here and it matches the price. I also just love how it looks. Disclaimer: I've played exactly one full run of this game. That experience led me to have almost no desire to continue playing, but maybe take this review with a grain of salt. On the other hand, I've spent thousands of hours playing dozens of roguelikes, so if that means anything, you can also consider that when taking my opinions into account. This is a well-made game. The designs and animations are charming. From strictly technical and surface perspectives, the individual aspects of this game are all fine. Even good, in most cases. The issues with Dicefolk come from the way the individual elements come together (or fail to); the far less tangible qualities that are critical to a good play experience: It fails in theme and feel. Theme is the easier and simpler of those to start with, so to say it outright, Dicefolk has the visible identity and nominal look of a creature battler/creature collector game. Of course, it's a roguelike, so one naturally understands that their team of creatures is going to be different every run, but instead of otherwise leaning into that identity (giving you lots of ways to train, upgrade, and improve your creatures), instead every creature is an interchangeable part of a game machine, and a core game mechanic constantly has you permanently throwing away earlier creatures in favor of ones you get later. The overall stats and the general power of the passive abilities improves with every area, and the creatures you start with have nothing special going for them, virtually guaranteeing you'll want to trade them out for better options as you go deeper into a run. This feels absolutely terrible. There's nothing specifically [i]wrong[/i] with it from a purely mechanical perspective, but the game actively discourages building emotional ties with your party of monsters fighting for you, and instead treats them like pieces of a machine you're meant to look at with cold isolation. On top of that, while the creatures are visually nice and well-animated, their designs leave a great deal to be desired when compared to industry leaders like Pokemon or Palworld. They lack features that give them a strongly-defined identity, and this issue actually carries over from visuals into mechanics. Many decisions feel like, "Would you like Creature A with 5 Attack and 28 Health, or Creature B with 6 attack and 25 Health? Their passives are vaguely different and neither one is useful to your current build." There just are not enough different types of stats to give creatures meaningful distinction the way you would want. The other place Dicefolk fails is in feel. There is a world of difference between a decision that [i]is[/i] impactful and a decision that [i]feels[/i] impactful. Whether people like or not, decisions that feel impactful are far more important for making a game feel good than decisions that actually are impactful. Ideally, decisions the player makes would be both, but when in doubt, it's far more beneficial to the play experience for them to genuinely feel important than to be important. As you no doubt already see where I'm going with this, Dicefolk is absolutely lacking in decisions that feel meaningful. You can already see it from the way I described choosing between one creature or another. While it's certainly true that many of these decisions can be significant in building a strong party, they rarely feel like this. The fact that the game gives the player an immense amount of control (backtracking within each area map, revisiting shops, etc.) only reinforces this. You leave a shop in Slay the Spire or Balatro, and it's gone for good. In Dicefolk, you can just sit on that decision until later if your current party is already strong enough, and make a better decision later. The game starts off painfully easy in the first run, and while I have no doubt that will appeal to many, it doesn't appeal to me in the slightest. I think, in general, a well-designed roguelike should have enough depth that it can start off very gently (giving everyone an easy way to get started) but should still provide room for challenge and thought within the first run. I just did not feel any resistance from the game. Maybe I was lucky; maybe I had amazing RNG and I'll never know, but I didn't even take damage in the last 33% of the run. The game looks pleasant and has no immediately obvious issues just from a quick look at a screenshot or a trailer, but it fails as a creature battler, makes all your decisions feel horrifically bland, and lacks any semblance of teeth as a roguelike. I take no joy in leaving this review, but I don't recommend it at all.

Dicefolk combines deckbuilder and creature collector to create an interesting experience. At all times, the game makes you feel in complete control: battle is decided by dice rolls, but you decide order of actions (including for opponent). Similarly, uncovering the map is non-linear and you will always see certain nodes (shops, upgrade stations) each run. This prevents a lot of RNG from ruining runs and this aspect is commendable. Unfortunately, despite randomness in creature attributes, equipment you find, etc., all of the runs feel basically the same. I honestly can't put my finger on why but it's probably a combination of a lot of little things. I've completed ~10 runs in different game modes and they no longer feel engaging.
